subject: anthropology
intro: Anthropology leads to paid work spent understanding people at close range — fieldwork and research posts, museum and archive jobs that steward what cultures leave behind, and university teaching.

roles.title: Anthropologists and Archeologists
roles.what: Study the origin, development and behaviour of human beings — the way of life, language and physical characteristics of peoples around the world — and some systematically recover and examine material remains of past cultures.
roles.where: The core-terms unit (culture, cultural relativism, agency) and the fieldwork unit on participant observation are the discipline's working toolkit; the societies-and-cultures-in-contact unit supplies the comparative perspective employers of anthropologists look for.

roles.title: Archivists
roles.what: Appraise, edit and direct the safekeeping of permanent records and historically valuable documents, and take part in research based on the archival materials in their care.
roles.where: The ethnographic-accounts unit — selecting, reading and judging representation in documents produced by observers — is directly what archivists do with records; the methods unit's qualitative and quantitative data training supports appraising what deserves permanent keeping.

roles.title: Curators
roles.what: Administer collections of artwork, collectibles, historic items or scientific specimens for museums and other institutions, and conduct the instructional, research and public-service activities that surround those collections.
roles.where: Coursework on ethnographic accounts and on how cultures are represented trains the judgement curators need to display other people's material culture fairly; the socialization and identity topics inform exhibition interpretation for the public.

roles.title: Anthropology and Archeology Teachers, Postsecondary
roles.what: Teach anthropology or archeology courses at colleges and universities — lecturing on kinship, culture and field method, running seminars, and usually combining teaching with their own field research.
roles.where: The IB units you follow here — core concepts, ethnography, methods and data collection — are the standard first-year course sequence these teachers deliver, and the fieldwork unit previews the research they do.
